finding: A Codex resume that never reaches idle spends the whole start budget, so the cleanup that follows gets no time and leaves the pane open.
why: The loop runs until deadline.expired(); _discard then calls call() with deadline.left()==0, which raises HerdrError('timeout') before any herdr command, so _agent_pid answers None and _close answers False without closing the pane; a stale or unknown resume session id reaches this path.
fix: Bound the resume wait like the agent-start path: stop waiting while deadline.left() > START_RESERVE_S, leaving the reserve for the discard.
evidence: herdr.py:196 `while not deadline.expired():` ; herdr.py:98-100 `budget = min(cap, deadline.left()) / if budget <= 0: raise HerdrError("timeout", ...)` ; herdr.py:328-329 `except HerdrError as error: return error.code in GONE`

finding: agent-read with since_marker likely returns empty text on a TUI pane: new output appears above an unchanged input-box footer, and the marker matches that footer at the end.
why: The marker hashes the last 3 non-empty lines, which on a Claude Code or Codex pane are the input box and status line; _after finds the same window again at the end and starts after it, so lines added above it are never returned.
fix: Anchor the marker on content above the TUI footer, or on a line count of the unwrapped history, and add a test whose screen ends in a constant footer.
evidence: herdr.py:378 `tail = [line for line in lines if line.strip()][-MARKER_LINES:]`; read-only check: lines ['● reply one', footer x4] then ['● reply one','● reply two','● reply three', footer x4] -> `_after` returns 7 of 7, text []

finding: On Windows the process tree adopts unrelated processes whose dead parent's id was reused by a member of the agent's tree, and kill_tree force-kills them.
why: Windows keeps a stale parent id after the parent exits; on this machine 33 live processes have a dead parent id, among them explorer.exe, WindowsTerminal.exe and msedge.exe, so any tree member that gets one of those ids drags that process and all its descendants into `taskkill /F`.
fix: In tree(), keep a child under a parent only when the child's creation time is not earlier than the parent's (GetProcessTimes), the standard Windows parent-id reuse guard.
evidence: process.py:185-187 `for child, parent in parents.items(): if child != parent: children.setdefault(parent, []).append(child)` with `_parents()` read from Toolhelp th32ParentProcessID; read-only check: `778 procs; 33 with dead parent pid` incl. ['explorer.exe','WindowsTerminal.exe','msedge.exe',...]

criterion: Acceptance bullet: each verb keeps its time budget (SDD §5)
finding: The multiplexer's herdr detection runs before the verb's Deadline starts and can take up to 20 s, outside the 10000 ms budgets of agent-status and agent-list.
why: `getattr(kind, ...)` triggers Multiplexer.tool() → herdr.detect(), which runs `herdr status` and `herdr integration status` with a 10 s timeout each, and only afterwards is `Deadline(verb)` built, so the detection time is never counted against the budget.
fix: Build the Deadline before resolving the kind's method, and give detection's herdr calls a timeout taken from that deadline.
evidence: contract.py:136-137 `method = getattr(kind, verb.replace("-", "_"))` / `code, body = 0, method(payload, Deadline(verb))`; herdr.py:78 `done = run(argv, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10, ...)`; contract bullet: "agent-status 10000 ms ... agent-list 10000 ms".

criterion: Acceptance bullet: every verb answers in the inherited shapes (SDD §3)
finding: contract.run catches only Answer, so any OSError or subprocess timeout inside a verb exits 1 with a Python traceback, which is none of the house answer shapes.
why: Reachable paths raise outside Answer: headless agent-start's `Path(log).parent.mkdir(...)` on an unwritable or file-occupied log folder (headless.py:65), and process.kill_tree's `taskkill` run with `timeout=15` (TimeoutExpired), so a caller gets exit 1 and no JSON.
fix: Map an unexpected exception in run() to an answer in the family's shapes (unavailable exit 4 with the reason, or stopped false for agent-stop), and add a test that forces one.
evidence: contract.py:138 `except Answer as answer:` is the only handler; headless.py:65 `Path(log).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`; ADAPTERS.md "Answer shapes" lists exits 0, 3, 4, 2 only.

finding: Possible: on Windows a harness installed as a .cmd shim (npm install) runs through cmd.exe, which cuts a multi-line prompt at the first line break and expands %VAR% and & inside it.
why: shutil.which can answer codex.cmd or claude.cmd, and the whole task prompt is the last argument of that command line.
fix: Refuse a .cmd/.bat binary with exit 4 naming it, or pass the prompt through a file or stdin for headless runs.
evidence: headless.py:367 `binary = shutil.which(run.binary)` ; headless.py:374-375 `"--", binary, *run.args]` ; launch.py:66-70 prompt is the last native argument

finding: A start whose job owner reports no pid within 15 s answers unavailable, but the owner keeps running and starts the agent, leaving an untracked headless run.
why: Nothing stops the spawned owner after the timeout, so a slow Python start (loaded Windows host) yields a running agent with no handle; a retry with the same log then shares the status file and can read the first run's pid.
fix: On the timeout path, kill the owner process (keep its Popen handle) and remove the status file before answering unavailable.
evidence: headless.py:374-382 `_spawn_owner([...])` ... `end = time.monotonic() + min(15.0, deadline.left())` ... `raise unavailable(... "the run's job owner reported no process in time")`

finding: Likely: on Windows each headless agent opens a visible console window, since the owner runs DETACHED_PROCESS and starts the console harness with no CREATE_NO_WINDOW.
why: A console program started by a process with no console gets a new console; the user can close that window and end the run, and every run pops one.
fix: Pass creationflags=0x08000000 (CREATE_NO_WINDOW) to the agent's Popen on Windows.
evidence: headless.py:349 `detached = 0x00000008 | 0x00000200          # DETACHED_PROCESS, CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` ; job.py:293-294 `subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=args.cwd, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)`

criterion: Acceptance bullet: SDD §7 'A failed kill answers stopped false' / SDD §3 agent-stop 'Never refuses'
finding: The multiplexer agent-stop refuses with exit 4 whenever herdr detection fails, so it neither kills the tree by process id nor answers stopped false.
why: Every verb, agent-stop included, goes through tool(), which runs detect(); a herdr server that does not answer `herdr status` (state broken), or a cleanup run from outside a herdr pane, turns agent-stop into exit 4 unavailable, though the process-id kill needs no herdr at all.
fix: Let agent_stop skip tool detection for the pid kill and answer pane_closed false naming the pane when no tool is usable, so the verb never refuses.
evidence: multiplexer.py: `def __getattr__ ... return getattr(self.tool(), name)` and `raise unavailable("no multiplexer tool is usable in this session (" ...`; SDD §3 agent-stop row: "Never refuses; a failure to stop is exit 0 with stopped false."

finding: On POSIX agent-stop never uses the session job.py leads, so a descendant reparented to init before the stop survives while stop answers stopped true.
why: kill_tree lists only current descendants by parent id; a background process whose shell already exited (for example `nohup server &` from the agent's shell) is no longer a descendant, yet CONTRACT.md promises the session as the POSIX job and lists no degradation.
fix: On POSIX also kill every process whose session id is the job owner's (record the owner pid or the sid in the status file and kill by sid), or document the gap under Documented degradation.
evidence: job.py:220 `Elsewhere: this owner leads its own session, which the agent and its children share.` ; process.py:202 `members = tree(pid)` ; headless/CONTRACT.md `## Documented degradation` `None.`

finding: The probe reads an unreadable configuration as no configuration and accepts an invalid forced kind with no conflict.
why: `afk-config.py get` loads without validating, so `transport.kind: panes` comes back as `panes` and resolve answers kind panes, conflict None (dispatch then raises ValueError); a malformed file exits 2 and the probe silently falls back to detection.
fix: Treat a non-zero exit other than 1 (absent) as a conflict naming the config file, and report a forced value outside KINDS as a conflict.
evidence: probe.py:41 `value = done.stdout.strip() if done.returncode == 0 else ""` ; probe.py:67-70 `problem = _forced_problem(...) ... return {**result, "kind": forced, ...}` ; afk-config.py:1470-1480 `get` uses `load(root)`, no `validate`

criterion: Acceptance bullet: each verb keeps its time budget (SDD §5; SDD §3 timeout column)
finding: A verb that runs past its budget makes dispatch raise TimeoutExpired, so probe.py crashes instead of giving SDD §3's after-timeout answer.
why: dispatch passes `timeout=seconds` (budget + 15 s) to subprocess.run and catches nothing, while SDD §3 says agent-start's timeout ends in 'unavailable' and agent-stop's in 'stopped false naming what survived'; nothing in the slice produces either answer.
fix: Catch TimeoutExpired in dispatch and answer the verb's timeout outcome in the house shape (exit 4 unavailable; for agent-stop exit 0 with stopped false), with a test.
evidence: probe.py:118-120 `seconds = contract.BUDGET_MS[verb] / 1000 + 15 ...` / `done = subprocess.run(..., timeout=seconds, env=child, check=False)`; SDD §3 agent-start row "| 120, then unavailable |", agent-stop row "| 60, then stopped false naming what survived |".

finding: The time-budget test only compares the BUDGET_MS constant table. No test shows that a verb stops at its budget, or that agent-start and agent-send make exactly one attempt.
why: The acceptance bullet covers behaviour. The test would still pass if Herdr.call ignored the Deadline, or if agent_send retried on a failure.
fix: Inject a fake clock or an expired Deadline and assert a timeout answer. In the FakeHerdr send test, fail `agent prompt` once and assert that exactly one `agent prompt` call was made.
evidence: Acceptance: "Each verb keeps its time budget ... agent-start and agent-send make 1 attempt with no automatic retry (SDD §5)"; test: `assert contract.BUDGET_MS == {"agent-start": 120000, ...}`

finding: No test proves the headless run is held by an operating-system job; the stop path kills by kill_tree, which works without any job.
why: Acceptance says the headless kind runs its agent under an operating-system job, but the only headless test ends the agent with process.kill_tree from its pid. A job.py that never called _join_job, or a POSIX owner without its own session, would still pass.
fix: Add a test that kills only the job.py owner, or checks IsProcessInJob on Windows and os.getsid(pid) on POSIX, then asserts the agent and its grandchild are gone.
evidence: Acceptance: "TR-2 runs its agent under an operating-system job (SDD §3)"; test lines 191-194: `headless("agent-stop", ...)` then `assert stop == {"stopped": True, "method": "killed the process tree"}`

finding: FakeHerdr replaces Herdr.call entirely, so no test covers how real herdr output is parsed into answers and error codes. The gone-pane, receiver_gone and idempotent-close branches all rest on herdr answer shapes the author wrote into the fake.
why: Herdr.call (herdr.py:97-120) reads the JSON `error.code` from stdout or stderr, unwraps `result`, and falls back to plain text. A herdr error printed in another shape would turn pane_not_found into a generic error: a second agent-stop would then answer pane_closed false, and agent-send would lose receiver_gone. Every multiplexer test would still pass.
fix: Add unit tests of Herdr.call against a stub herdr binary (or a monkeypatched subprocess.run) that replays recorded herdr 0.9.1 output: a success with `result`, a pane_not_found error object, and plain-text `pane read`.
evidence: `monkeypatch.setattr(herdr.Herdr, "call", lambda self, args, deadline, cap=30.0: session.handle(args))`

finding: The V31 seam test passes whatever the partial installer does: no herdr binary exists anywhere on the probe's PATH, and there is no positive control.
why: The C15 probe is `herdr --version`, and the re-probe PATH holds only the stub dir and an empty .herdr. The probe fails with or without the stub install, so the test cannot tell 'a part-way install is detected as not fixed' from 'the probe always fails in this environment'.
fix: Add a control where a complete stub install puts a working `herdr` on that PATH and the same probe exits 0. Make the part-way stub leave a herdr file that cannot run, or no link on PATH, so the stub actually decides the outcome.
evidence: MANIFEST.md C15 `- **Probe:** `herdr --version``; test: `env={"PATH": f"{stub}{os.pathsep}{home / '.herdr'}", ...}` then `assert reprobe.returncode != 0`

criterion: Acceptance bullet: ADAPTERS.md documents the transport family (ADR-0001), judged against D-63
finding: ADAPTERS.md says configuration never sets AFK_CFG_TRANSPORT, which contradicts D-63 and the slice's own MANIFEST env row.
why: D-63 records that an empty `transport:` section exports AFK_CFG_TRANSPORT as '' (it superseded D-43's premise that no configuration sets it), and MANIFEST.md says the same, so the family doc restates the premise D-63 withdrew.
fix: Reword to: the kind sits at `transport.kind`; only an empty `transport:` section exports AFK_CFG_TRANSPORT, as '', and the probe sets the kind after its load.
evidence: ADAPTERS.md:209-210 "The kind sits at `transport.kind`, so configuration never sets `AFK_CFG_TRANSPORT`."; DECISIONS.md D-63 "Supersedes: D-43's premise that no configuration sets AFK_CFG_TRANSPORT — an empty `transport:` section sets it to ''".

criterion: a signature/rename whose call sites are not all updated
finding: Reworded gate-coverage sentence leaves the gate's own pointer text calling "Adding a kind" the list of the four checked places.
why: The line now says the gate checks steps 1 to 3 only, but hooks/skill-registry-gate.sh:235 still sends a failing developer to this list as "the four", and hooks/lib/adapter_registry_check.py:10 numbers its four places against it, which no longer match steps 1 to 4.
fix: Make the two readers say the gate checks "steps 1 to 3" of "Adding a kind", in the same change, or put the old wording back.
evidence: ADAPTERS.md:228 "`skill-registry-gate.sh` fails until steps 1 to 3 exist; nothing checks step 4." vs hooks/skill-registry-gate.sh:235 "Adapter described in some places but not all (ADAPTERS.md \"Adding a kind\" lists the four):"

finding: A read that stops at the 1 MiB cap or at the live end can split a UTF-8 character, giving replacement characters on both sides of the marker.
why: The marker is a raw byte offset and the chunk is decoded with errors='replace'.
fix: Back the end offset up to the last complete UTF-8 sequence before decoding.
evidence: headless.py:417-419 `chunk = handle.read(READ_CAP)` ... `"text": chunk.decode("utf-8", "replace"), "marker": str(end)`

finding: On Windows the final status write can fail while agent-status is reading the file, losing the exit code.
why: os.replace onto a file another process has open without delete sharing raises PermissionError, and job.py has no retry, so it dies before recording exit_code.
fix: Retry os.replace a few times on PermissionError.
evidence: job.py:237-239 `tmp.write_text(...)` / `os.replace(tmp, path)` ; headless.py:339 `return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))`

finding: A tab name whose last word is a number never matches its own tab, so every start opens a new tab; a successor label can also repeat.
why: _tab_group('round 2') is 'round', not 'round 2', so `ours` is empty and the label is the tab name again; with 'x' closed and 'x 2' full, len(ours)+1 makes another 'x 2'.
fix: Strip the number only when the head equals the requested tab name, and number a successor from the highest number in use.
evidence: herdr.py:357-358 `head, _, tail = label.rpartition(" ") / return head if head and tail.isdigit() else label` ; herdr.py:172 `label = tab if not ours else f"{tab} {len(ours) + 1}"`

finding: Every resolve_kind test fakes the configuration reader. No test of the forced-kind or pane-switch path runs the real `afk-config.py get transport.kind` against a real .afk/config.yaml.
why: The fake returns exactly the value the test puts in and ignores the cwd that _config passes. A wrong key name, a wrong cwd, or a reader exit 2 on bad config (read as absent) would go unnoticed.
fix: Add one resolve_kind test that writes a repo_with config forcing `transport.kind: headless`, uses the real subprocess.run for the config call, and fakes only herdr's commands.
evidence: `if any(str(a).endswith("afk-config.py") for a in argv): value = self.config.get(argv[-1])`

finding: One headless test covers start, status, read, read-since-marker, stop, status after the stop, and a repeat stop (an eager test).
why: A failure points at one test with 7 behaviours inside, and its 300 s stub processes are left running when an early assert fails, because there is no cleanup.
fix: Split into a start-and-status test, a read-and-marker test and a stop-and-idempotency test, sharing a fixture that kills the tree in teardown.
evidence: lines 177-198: agent-start, agent-status, agent-read, agent-read since_marker, agent-stop, agent-status, agent-stop in one body

finding: The V31 proof of setup's 'not fixed' rule matches a prose line together with its exact line wrap and indent.
why: Re-wrapping SKILL.md step 5 breaks the test without any change of behaviour, and the test reads prose, not setup's output.
fix: Normalize whitespace before matching, as test_c15_skips_with_no_human_reprobes_and_prints_a_removal_line already does for its own match.
evidence: `assert "A fix not flipping its probe to exit 0\n   is not fixed" in step5`
